body:
DECIDED BY MYK IN CHAT, 2026-08-19 (late), reasoning through the containment model with the
session. Two related pieces, both deliberately NOT built tonight.

PIECE 1 — NAMING A DESCENDANT. The base gather excludes descendants (see T189 for why: quarantine
leak, isolation-by-etiquette, and a new container silently changing what existing queries answer).
Descent is therefore an EXPLICIT act, and the API already has the right shape:

    containerScope({ containers: ["A", "A.1"] })

You name what you want. What is missing is the RIGHTS half: naming a container you may not read must
refuse, and it must refuse in the uniform shape that does not disclose whether the container exists
(SPEC 12 / T78's mount-existence oracle is the precedent — the same reasoning applies to containers,
and for the same reason).

Reachability and permission stay SEPARATE concerns. That separation is what makes multi-tenancy work:
the operator CAN name tenant B, and whether they may read it is a grant question rather than a gather
question. Collapsing the two would either make the operator omniscient or make containers unreachable
by their own owners.

PIECE 2 — OPERATOR AS SUDO (Myk: "operator could be kinda like sudo?"). A store operator is today an
ambient property of an identity: gw.operatorAuthor is consulted everywhere, and operator-ness applies
to every request that identity makes. Myk wants the distinction between ACTING AS MY USER and ACTING
AS THE OPERATOR — one identity, two capacities, with the elevated one an EXPLICIT act rather than an
ambient condition.

Why it matters beyond ergonomics: ambient authority means the operator's ordinary reads carry
constitutional power they did not ask for, so every accident is an accident with maximum privilege.
An explicit elevation makes the powerful act visible in the record — a delta says "this was done as
operator" — which is what an audit needs and what an ambient property can never provide.

NOT SCOPED YET. This ticket records the decision and the reasoning so neither is re-derived. Piece 1
is buildable once T189 lands (it shares the scoped-read path). Piece 2 is design-stage and wants its
own working spec with user stories, because it changes what an identity IS.

A THIRD THING, NAMED SO IT IS NOT CONFUSED WITH PIECE 1: "the operator cannot read tenant B at all"
is a STRONGER property than "the operator is refused by policy". It needs the refusal to be
unforgeable rather than enforced — encryption at the container boundary, not a grant check. Myk
flagged it as worth a ticket someday. It is not this ticket, and a policy check must never be
described as if it were that guarantee (H7).
title: Naming a descendant container, and the operator/user split (sudo)
